title: Icelandic cast-off
subtitle: A stretchy cast-off for shoulder joins in yoke construction.
excerpt: The Icelandic cast-off uses short rows to create a cast-off with built-in ease at shoulder seams. A traditional technique from Fair Isle and Icelandic yoke knitting where the shoulder must lie flat without pulling.
sourceNotes: Traditional technique associated with Icelandic and Faroese yoke construction. Referenced in comparative stitch literature; related to the Shetland and Fair Isle shoulder methods documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1886). Not reproduced verbatim from any in-copyright source.

glossaryTerms.definition: A shoulder cast-off technique that works short rows into the front and back sets of live stitches to ease the shoulder seam before closing it. Prevents the classic pulling that afflicts standard cast-offs on set-in sleeves.

content.text: combines a short-row wedge with a standard cast-off to produce a shoulder join that lies flat and accommodates the natural slope of the shoulder. Traditional Icelandic lopi yoke sweaters use it to close the front and back yoke stitches across the shoulder without the pulled, bunched look that a straight cast-off creates when the shoulder is sloped. Difficulty: intermediate.
Two needle tips holding the front and back shoulder stitches
Hold the front and back shoulder stitches on parallel needle tips, right sides facing each other.
Work the first third of the shoulder stitches using the three-needle cast-off. Place a marker.
Turn the work. Slip the marker. Work back across to the armhole edge, purling the uncast-off stitches.
Turn the work again. Work the three-needle cast-off across all remaining shoulder stitches.

Traditional Icelandic lopi sweater patterns use this technique at each shoulder. It appears in Scandinavian and Fair Isle pattern books and in reconstructed Shetland garments. When a pattern says 'shape shoulder with short rows before joining', this is the technique it means.

items.symptom: Shoulder seam still pulls toward the neck
items.cause: Not working enough short-row ease before the final cast-off
items.fix: Work two short-row turns rather than one, placing each marker one third of the way across rather than at the half-point.

items.cause: Not wrapping or working a German short row at the turn
items.fix: At each turn, work a wrap-and-turn or the German short-row double stitch to close the gap.
